# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

# Documentation
To verify that documentation changes don't alter the generated output:

136	### 4.2 driver 协调循环
137	
138	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
139	
140	`driver.py` 的 `train()` 是**一次训练尝试（attempt）**的协调者。它自己不执行模型前向、不搬运权重——那些属于钉死的 MILES 运行时（SGLang 推理引擎 + OLMo-core 训练器）。driver 的职责是把各角色连起来并在正确的时机放置边界：
141	
142	- rollout 收集（推理引擎按当前策略采样）；
143	- 优化器更新（训练器消费一个 batch）；
144	- 权重发布（把训练器的新权重推给推理引擎，支持 barrier / refresh / engine-drain 三种模式）；
145	- 存档边界（周期存档、最终存档、哨兵文件触发）；
146	- 评估与后台评估的分发；
147	- 无论成功失败都要做的有序清理。
148	
149	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
150	
151	`driver.train` 的主干可以概括成下面的伪代码（省略 async 细节）：
152	
153	```text
154	train(args):
155	    解析时间预算 max_run_seconds → deadline；判定时间停是否可恢复(resumable)
156	    启动 Ray → 初始化 W&B → 启动 worker manager
157	    （colocate/offload 时序约束下）启动 serving 与 trainer；拿到 rollouts_per_epoch
158	    首次权重发布 publish()；等待 judge 就绪
159	    for rollout_id in range(start_rollout_id, num_rollout):     # ← 主循环
160	        batch = manager.get(rollout_id)            # 池耗尽则存档并 break
161	        learner.train(rollout_id, batch)           # 优化器更新
162	        completed.append(rollout_id)
163	        若满足存档条件: manager.save + learner.save_model + finalize_checkpoint
164	        若 refresh 模式 / 到更新间隔: publish(rollout_id)
165	        若到评估间隔: evaluation.dispatch(rollout_id)
166	        若到时间预算: break（resumable 与否决定 final_stop）
167	        若 debug_exit_after_rollout 达到: break
168	    收尾：评估 drain、最终 HF 导出、后台评估 final 分发
169	    finally：按序清理（prepared batch → 生成停止 → 权重传输关闭 → 各角色 dispose）
170	    return {completed_rollout_ids, num_rollout, pools_exhausted, ...}
171	```
172	
173	存档条件的判定（对应 [driver.py:299-317](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L299-L317)）是四项的析取：
174	
175	\[
176	\text{save} \iff (\text{到时且可存}) \ \lor\ \text{sentinel} \ \lor\ (\text{save\_final\_checkpoint} \land \text{最后一个 rollout}) \ \lor\ \text{周期 interval 到达}
177	\]

221	### 4.3 完成判定与最终存档：epoch 预算如何被判定为 complete（本轮更新重点）
222	
223	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
224	
225	本轮代码更新（896a734 → bae4209）引入了 **epoch 预算**：研究者可以用 `training.num_epoch = N` 声明「把数据训 N 遍」，而不必先算出这对应多少个 rollout。这带来两个必须解决的工程问题：
226	
227	1. **完成判定**：workflow 之前拿 `config.miles["num_rollout"]` 与完成计数比对。epoch 预算的编译产物里**故意没有** `num_rollout`（数据集没加载，总数未知），旧的比较永远比不出「到达终点」。解法：原生运行时在数据加载后把解析出的总数写回 `args.num_rollout`，driver 在返回字典里带上它，workflow 优先使用返回值。
228	2. **最终存档**：rollout 预算的 run 靠 `save_interval`（默认等于 `num_rollout`，即只在结尾存一次）拿到最终权重；epoch 预算没有这个锚点，于是新增 `core.save_final_checkpoint`，由编译器默认置真，driver 在最后一个 rollout 落盘。

230	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
231	
232	```text
233	TOML [training] num_epoch=2
234	   │ run_spec.py L551 兜底 put("miles.num_epoch")   （num_epoch 不在 FIELD_MAP/CORE_FIELDS）

322	### 4.4 Supervisor 启动监管
323	
324	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
325	
326	`cluster.py` 回答的问题是：**「一个 Beaker 副本内，如何把 Ray、judge 服务和训练 workflow 安全地拉起来，并在任何一方挂掉时让全体有序失败？」** `Supervisor` 是每个副本各一个的监管线程 + 子进程管理者，它提供四样东西：
327	
328	- **启动预算（startup budget）**：rank 0 发布一个统一的 deadline，所有后续启动工作（inventory、judge、Ray、workflow）共享这一个时钟；
329	- **心跳**：每 2 秒写 `heartbeat-{rank}.json` 并检查对端心跳，超时即失败——这是「对端节点消失」的检测器；
330	- **子进程监管**：被监管子进程非零退出、judge 连续 3 次健康探针失败，都会让本副本失败；
331	- **失败可见化**：失败写 `failed-{rank}.json`，对端在 `check()` 里发现即跟着失败。
332	
333	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
334	
335	```text
336	run(config)                                  # 每个 Beaker 副本一个进程
337	  ├─ 编译 + topology.plan；校验副本数/排名与提交一致
338	  ├─ rendezvous.join(output.root/cluster/<attempt>, rank, count)
339	  │    → 每次启动进入全新 attempt 目录（旧的 attempt 留档）
340	  ├─ Supervisor(...)：rank0 写 startup.json（唯一 deadline）；其余副本等它出现
341	  ├─ 心跳线程启动；SIGTERM/SIGINT → 抛错（让清理路径执行）
342	  ├─ 各副本写 node-{rank}.json → 等全部到齐 → topology.assign 得到本机分工
343	  ├─ GPU inventory 校验（可见设备数 == 计划数）；rollout GPU 还要过 profile 硬件校验
344	  ├─ 按分工起 judge 服务（各占自己的 GPU），端点写盘；head 额外占 3 个 Ray 端口
345	  ├─ ray start --block（head 带 --head，worker 带 --address）
346	  └─ head：start_workflow（ray-readiness/judge-readiness 两个探针任务 + driver 子进程）
347	     其余：等 complete.json → 各写 done-{rank}.json → head 收到全部 done 后收尾
348	```
349

354	**心跳线程**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:109-154](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L109-L154)：每 2 秒写自己的心跳、检查对端心跳与子进程、按需探针 judge 健康。`check_peer_heartbeats` 有两个值得注意的细节：共享文件系统上的瞬时缺文件不算对端死亡（保留最后一次观测值，但不延长其期限）；心跳超过 `heartbeat_timeout` 即抛错。被监管子进程退出码非零同样抛错——但仅当 `complete.json` 还不存在（训练完成后的退出不是故障）。

392	## 5. 综合实践
393	
394	把本讲四个模块串成一份「run 生命周期 Runbook」。产物是一份 Markdown 笔记，包含三部分：
395	
396	**任务 A：三阶段输入输出表**。对照 `execute`（[workflow.py:349-426](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L349-L426)）与 [docs/miles/workflow.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/workflow.md)，填写：

399	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
400	| 模型准备 | `model.source`（HF 或 native） | `<conversion.hf_output>` + `workflow-model.json` | 身份一致即复用 | `model_identity` 清单 |
401	| 数据准备 | `data` + HF 目录 | `prepared/data/` + manifest | （结合 u8-l4 的清单与标记） | ? |
402	| 训练 | `RunConfig` + resume checkpoint | `checkpoints/`、`rollouts/`、`workflow.json` | 从 `core-latest.json` 续训 | 指纹 + `clock.next_rollout_id` |
403	
404	并用自己的话回答：**中断后哪些阶段可跳过、哪些必须重算？**（要点：指纹匹配 + 产物标记完整 → 模型/数据直接复用；训练阶段从最新 checkpoint 恢复，未消费的提示组再生。）

412	```

416	## 6. 本讲小结
417	
418	- `workflow.execute` 把一次 run 分成准备/训练/收尾三阶段；run 身份 = 规格字典排序 JSON 的 SHA-256，resume 时只有运维字段（重试、缓存、存档/评估节奏）允许变动，模型/数据/训练视野必须严格一致。

# 工作流与执行：driver、workflow 与集群启动

> 本讲对应 MILES 单元第三讲。上一讲（u8-l2）我们已经看过 TOML run 文件如何被 `RunSpec` 「加载即编译」成 `RunConfig`；本讲顺着这条链往下走：**编译产物交给谁、在 GPU 集群上如何被执行、中断之后如何恢复、以及一次 run 何时才算「完成」**。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出一次 MILES run 的三个阶段（准备 / 训练 / 导出）各自的输入输出，以及哪些阶段在中断后可以复用、哪些必须重算。
2. 解释「指纹（fingerprint）」如何支撑 resume：配置身份如何计算、哪些字段的改动被允许、哪些会被拒绝。
3. 读懂 `driver.train` 的协调循环：rollout 收集 → 优化器更新 → 权重发布 → 存档边界，以及时间停 / debug 退出 / 池耗尽三种提前退出方式。
4. **掌握本轮更新的核心变化**：run 完成判定改用 driver 返回值中的 `num_rollout`；`training.num_epoch` 预算的 run 由原生运行时在数据加载后才解析出 rollout 总数，并通过 `core.save_final_checkpoint` 在最后一次更新时落盘最终存档。
5. 理解 `cluster.Supervisor` 如何在 Beaker 副本内做受监管启动（心跳、健康探针、启动预算）。

## 2. 前置知识

- **run 文件与 RunSpec（承接 u8-l2）**：一份 TOML 描述模型、数据、训练器、推理引擎与集群分配；`RunSpec.compile()` 把结构化小节翻译成 `CoreConfig`（经 `--olmo-core-config` 传入）和原生 MILES 参数（`--num-rollout`、`--num-epoch` 等）。本讲只取其中与「训练预算」和「存档节奏」相关的编译产出。
- **rollout（采样回合）**：GRPO 类算法以「一轮采样 + 若干次优化器更新」为基本节奏。一轮收集 `rollout_batch_size × n_samples_per_prompt` 条回答，`global_batch_size` 决定每次更新消耗多少条。
- **幂等与指纹**：分布式训练会被抢占、被重启。为了让重启后的进程能安全复用上一轮的产物，系统给每个产物记录「身份」（输入的哈希或清单），重启时先核对身份，一致才复用——这就是指纹。
- **Beaker 副本（replica）**：MILES 的多机 run 会被 Beaker 调成多个副本，每个副本在各自节点上跑一个 `cluster` 进程；其中 IP 最小的节点成为 head，只有 head 运行训练 workflow。
- **原生运行时（pinned MILES runtime）**：open-instruct 通过 `--miles` 镜像使用一版钉死的 MILES/Core 运行时。数据集加载、rollout 引擎与优化器执行都发生在那个运行时里；open-instruct 侧的 driver 只做编排。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py) | 一次 run 的总编排：模型/数据准备、身份记录、run 目录锁、训练调用与完成判定 |
| [open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py) | 单次训练尝试的协调循环：rollout、更新、发布、存档、清理，并返回结果字典 |
| [open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py) | Beaker 副本内的 `Supervisor`：rendezvous、心跳、judge 健康探针、Ray 启动与 workflow 拉起 |
| [open_instruct/miles/execution/timing.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/timing.py) | `stage()` 上下文管理器：把 driver 各阶段耗时写成 `driver_timing.jsonl` |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py) | 编译链中与本讲相关的两处：`num_epoch`/`num_rollout` 预算选择、`save_final_checkpoint` 默认值 |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py) | `CoreConfig.save_final_checkpoint` 字段定义与 `num_epoch` 正整数校验 |
| [open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py) | epoch 预算编译行为的单测（本讲实践的验证工具） |
| [docs/miles/workflow.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/workflow.md) | 研究者视角的工作流文档：plan/validate/train/run/status 与恢复语义 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 workflow 阶段与指纹恢复

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`workflow.py` 回答的问题是：**「一份 run 规格，如何变成磁盘上一组可恢复的产物？」** 它把一次 run 划分为三个阶段：

1. **准备（prepare）**：把模型源转换/暂存成 HF 目录、把数据准备成带验证目标的提示集，并给两个产物各写一份「身份清单」。
2. **训练（train）**：把编译好的配置交给 driver（见 4.2）执行。
3. **导出/收尾**：driver 返回结果字典，workflow 据此把 run 状态写成 `complete` 或 `stopped`。

「指纹」是这一切的安全网：run 目录里记录了启动时规格的哈希，重启时新规格必须与记录匹配（或在允许的「运维字段」上等价），否则拒绝恢复，逼你换一个新的 `output.root`。这防止了「换数据续训旧目录」这类静默事故。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
execute(spec)
  │
  ├─ run_directory(spec)            # 独占锁 + 身份校验 + attempt 记账
  │    ├─ flock(.workflow.lock)     # 多进程互斥
  │    ├─ fingerprint(spec) == 旧 spec_sha256 ?  # 否则按白名单归一化后再比
  │    ├─ 旧 status == complete ? → 拒绝（已完成 run 不可覆盖）
  │    └─ auto_resume=false 且目录已存在 ? → 拒绝
  │
  ├─ 阶段1 准备：prepare_model → prepare_data → 判分注册表校验
  │    （模型/数据产物带身份清单，resume 时直接复用）
  │
  ├─ 阶段2 训练：auto_resume 且有 core-latest.json → 挂载 load；
  │    train_config() → parse_runtime() → driver.train()
  │
  └─ 阶段3 收尾：按结果字典判定 complete / stopped，写 workflow.json
```

指纹的数学定义很直接——对规格字典做「按键排序后的 JSON 序列化」再取 SHA-256：

\[
\mathrm{fingerprint}(d) = \mathrm{SHA256}\big(\mathrm{json\_dumps}(d,\ \mathrm{sort\_keys}=\text{true})\big)
\]

注意 `sort_keys=True` 保证了同一逻辑规格（字典键顺序不同）得到同一指纹。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**run 目录的锁与身份校验**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:306-346](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L306-L346) 是 `run_directory` 上下文管理器：先用 `fcntl.flock` 对 `.workflow.lock` 加非阻塞独占锁（防止两个进程同时写同一 run 目录）；然后计算当前规格的指纹，与 `workflow.json` 里记录的 `spec_sha256` 比对；若旧状态是 `complete` 直接拒绝（完成的 run 不可覆盖）；若 `launch.auto_resume=false` 且目录已有 workflow 也拒绝。任何阶段抛异常时，把状态更新为 `failed` 并记录错误再上抛。

**指纹计算（含 OPD 历史兼容）**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:38-44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L38-L44) 在哈希前对 OPD 算法的 run 做了两处剔除（空的 `miles` 覆盖表、`keep_checkpoints`），让历史上可选的字段不改变 run 身份。

**允许 resume 时改动的字段白名单**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:58-97](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L58-L97) 的 `recovery_configuration_matches`：先严格比对原始哈希；不一致时读取磁盘上的 `run-spec.json` 做认证（记录的规格也要能算出旧指纹，防篡改），然后把**运维性字段**从新规格「领养」进记录再比较——包括 `launch.auto_resume` / `max_retries` / `memory`、编译器缓存各项、`training.save_interval` 与 `evaluation.interval`。换句话说：**恢复策略、缓存位置、存档/评估节奏可以改；模型、数据、训练视野（horizon）、算法配方不能改**。

**重启记账**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:107-128](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L107-L128) 的 `record_attempt`：Beaker 对被抢占任务会无限重启，一个总在存档前被抢占的 run 会永远空转。每次启动向 `attempts.json` 追加一条记录，超过 `launch.max_retries` 即拒绝再启动（`-1` 关闭上限，且「重试次数」不含首次启动）。

**模型身份清单与准备复用**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:131-149](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L131-L149) 的 `model_identity` 不对几十 GB 的权重做哈希，而是记录每个文件的路径、大小、纳秒级 mtime，仅对小文件（`.json` / `.jinja` / `.metadata`）算 SHA-256；[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:179-190](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L179-L190) 里 `prepare_model` 用目标目录下的 `workflow-model.json` 标记：身份一致且产物清单完整 → 直接复用；身份变化或目录不完整 → 报错要求换新 `output.root`。数据准备（`prepare_data`，见 u8-l4）走同样的「清单 + 标记」思路。

**三阶段总编排**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:349-426](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L349-L426) 的 `execute`：

- L352-353 `prepare_model`（阶段一·模型），L356-378 `prepare_data` + 判分注册表校验（阶段一·数据）；
- L396-398：`auto_resume=true` 且 checkpoint 目录存在 `core-latest.json` 时，把它挂到 `config.miles["load"]`，实现「从最新完成的 Core checkpoint 续训」；
- L399-403：写 `resolved-plan.json`、发 ad­visories，状态改为 `training`；
- L404-412：调用 `train_config`（内含 `parse_runtime` 与 `driver.train`，见 4.2/4.3）；
- L413-423：完成判定（本讲更新重点，见 4.3.3）。

**训练前的运行时解析**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:267-303](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L267-L303)：`parse_runtime` 临时替换 `sys.argv` 调用原生 MILES 的 `parse_args`，并要求后端必须是 `olmo_core`；若带 `--load` 恢复，则从 checkpoint 的 resume manifest 里取出 `clock.next_rollout_id` 作为 `start_rollout_id`——这就是「rollout 游标不重不漏」的来源。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不改任何代码，梳理一次 run 会在 `output.root` 里留下哪些文件，并验证 CPU 侧的配置检查可用。

1. 通读 `execute`（上文链接），把下表填完整（参考要点见第 5 节综合实践的任务 A）：

   | 文件 | 写入者（函数/行号） | 阶段 | resume 时的用途 |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `run-spec.json` | ? | ? | ? |
   | `plan.json` / `resolved-plan.json` | ? | ? | ? |
   | `workflow.json` | ? | ? | ? |
   | `attempts.json` | ? | ? | ? |
   | `prepared/`、`checkpoints/`、`inference-profile.json` | ? | ? | ? |

2. 在仓库根目录运行（CPU 即可，不需要 GPU/WEKA）：

   ```bash
   python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/dev.toml
   python -m open_instruct.miles validate configs/miles/examples/dev.toml
   ```

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `recovery_configuration_matches` 允许改 `training.save_interval`，却不允许改 `training.num_epoch`？
**答案**：`save_interval` 只影响「未来产物的节奏」，不改变已经训出的权重语义；而 `num_epoch` 属于训练视野（horizon）——改了它等于改变这次 run 要训多少数据，与目录里已记录的指纹身份冲突。源码注释明确写了「Keep training horizon, evaluation tasks/scorers, and all recipe fields strict」（[workflow.py:86-88](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L86-L88)）。

**答案**：`record_attempt` 读到 `attempts.json` 已有 3 条记录，`len(attempts) > limit`（3 > 2）成立，抛出 `InputError`，提示要么调大 `launch.max_retries` 要么换新 `output.root`（[workflow.py:119-125](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L119-L125)）。注意上限按「重启次数」计，首次启动不会被拒。

**答案**：权重动辄几十 GB，每次启动都全量哈希会把恢复拖慢到不可用。它退而记录（路径, 大小, mtime_ns）三元组，只对小体积的配置/模板文件做内容哈希——以极小概率漏检「同大小同时间的权重替换」换取可用的启动速度（[workflow.py:131-149](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L131-L149)，函数 docstring 自述 "without hashing tens of GB"）。

### 4.2 driver 协调循环

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`driver.py` 的 `train()` 是**一次训练尝试（attempt）**的协调者。它自己不执行模型前向、不搬运权重——那些属于钉死的 MILES 运行时（SGLang 推理引擎 + OLMo-core 训练器）。driver 的职责是把各角色连起来并在正确的时机放置边界：

- rollout 收集（推理引擎按当前策略采样）；
- 优化器更新（训练器消费一个 batch）；
- 权重发布（把训练器的新权重推给推理引擎，支持 barrier / refresh / engine-drain 三种模式）；
- 存档边界（周期存档、最终存档、哨兵文件触发）；
- 评估与后台评估的分发；
- 无论成功失败都要做的有序清理。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`driver.train` 的主干可以概括成下面的伪代码（省略 async 细节）：

```text
train(args):
    解析时间预算 max_run_seconds → deadline；判定时间停是否可恢复(resumable)
    启动 Ray → 初始化 W&B → 启动 worker manager
    （colocate/offload 时序约束下）启动 serving 与 trainer；拿到 rollouts_per_epoch
    首次权重发布 publish()；等待 judge 就绪
    for rollout_id in range(start_rollout_id, num_rollout):     # ← 主循环
        batch = manager.get(rollout_id)            # 池耗尽则存档并 break
        learner.train(rollout_id, batch)           # 优化器更新
        completed.append(rollout_id)
        若满足存档条件: manager.save + learner.save_model + finalize_checkpoint
        若 refresh 模式 / 到更新间隔: publish(rollout_id)
        若到评估间隔: evaluation.dispatch(rollout_id)
        若到时间预算: break（resumable 与否决定 final_stop）
        若 debug_exit_after_rollout 达到: break
    收尾：评估 drain、最终 HF 导出、后台评估 final 分发
    finally：按序清理（prepared batch → 生成停止 → 权重传输关闭 → 各角色 dispose）
    return {completed_rollout_ids, num_rollout, pools_exhausted, ...}
```

存档条件的判定（对应 [driver.py:299-317](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L299-L317)）是四项的析取：

\[
\text{save} \iff (\text{到时且可存}) \ \lor\ \text{sentinel} \ \lor\ (\text{save\_final\_checkpoint} \land \text{最后一个 rollout}) \ \lor\ \text{周期 interval 到达}
\]

### 4.3 完成判定与最终存档：epoch 预算如何被判定为 complete（本轮更新重点）

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

本轮代码更新（896a734 → bae4209）引入了 **epoch 预算**：研究者可以用 `training.num_epoch = N` 声明「把数据训 N 遍」，而不必先算出这对应多少个 rollout。这带来两个必须解决的工程问题：

1. **完成判定**：workflow 之前拿 `config.miles["num_rollout"]` 与完成计数比对。epoch 预算的编译产物里**故意没有** `num_rollout`（数据集没加载，总数未知），旧的比较永远比不出「到达终点」。解法：原生运行时在数据加载后把解析出的总数写回 `args.num_rollout`，driver 在返回字典里带上它，workflow 优先使用返回值。
2. **最终存档**：rollout 预算的 run 靠 `save_interval`（默认等于 `num_rollout`，即只在结尾存一次）拿到最终权重；epoch 预算没有这个锚点，于是新增 `core.save_final_checkpoint`，由编译器默认置真，driver 在最后一个 rollout 落盘。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
TOML [training] num_epoch=2
   │ run_spec.py L551 兜底 put("miles.num_epoch")   （num_epoch 不在 FIELD_MAP/CORE_FIELDS）
   ▼
miles.num_epoch=2，且 miles.num_rollout 不存在
   │ L735-739：两者同设 → InputError；只设 epoch → 不再默认补 num_rollout=100
   ▼
L780-787：save_checkpoints=true（默认）且无 num_rollout
   → core.save_final_checkpoint = True（不发明周期 save_interval）
   ▼
RunConfig.arguments()：--num-epoch 2（无 --num-rollout）；
save_final_checkpoint 随 --olmo-core-config JSON 进入 args.olmo_core
   ▼
原生运行时加载数据集 → 解析 num_epoch 为 num_rollout（写入 args.num_rollout）
   ▼
driver 主循环跑满 num_rollout：L304 在最后一个 rollout 存档
   ▼
driver 返回 {"num_rollout": args.num_rollout, ...}
   ▼
workflow.execute：completed[-1]+1 == result["num_rollout"] → status=complete
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**预算二选一**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:735-739](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L735-L739)：`num_epoch` 与 `num_rollout` 同时设置直接 `InputError`（"Choose num_epoch or num_rollouts; MILES would otherwise ignore num_epoch"——防止用户以为 epoch 生效实际被忽略）；只设 `num_epoch` 时**不再**补默认 `num_rollout=100`（旧版这个默认值无条件写入，正是 epoch 预算此前不可用的原因）。

**存档节奏的编译**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:780-792](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L780-L792)：`save_checkpoints=true` 时——有 `num_rollout` 则 `save_interval` 默认取它（只在结尾存）；否则（epoch 预算）`core.setdefault("save_final_checkpoint", True)`，注释写明「Native MILES resolves the epoch budget after loading the dataset. Save the final update without inventing a periodic cadence here.」`save_checkpoints=false` 与显式 `save_interval` 冲突报错；与 `max_run_seconds` 组合则把时间停标记为终局（`max_run_final=True`，无可恢复之物）。

**新 CoreConfig 字段**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py:72-73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L72-L73)：`save_final_checkpoint: bool = False`，注释定位为「epoch 派生预算、无周期存档节奏时的 driver 策略」；它在 [config.py:226-243](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L226-L243) 的布尔字段校验表中，并经 [config.py:801-822](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L801-L822) 的 `arguments()` 随 `--olmo-core-config` 的 JSON 传给运行时，最终出现在 driver 眼中的 `args.olmo_core.save_final_checkpoint`。`num_epoch` 的正整数校验在 [config.py:635-637](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L635-L637)（`0`、负数、`true` 都被拒——注意 Python 里 `True` 是 `int`，所以这里显式检查 `type(...) is not int`）。

**driver 侧的最终存档与返回值**（已在 4.2.3 展开，这里只点名）：[driver.py:304](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L304) 的第三个存档触发条件与 [driver.py:430-438](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L430-L438) 返回字典中的 `num_rollout`。

**workflow 的完成判定**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py:413-423](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L413-L423)：

```python
completed = result.get("completed_rollout_ids") if result else None
complete = (
    completed is None
    or bool(result.get("pools_exhausted"))
    or (bool(result.get("stopped_for_time")) and not result.get("time_stop_resumable"))
    or (
        (completed[-1] + 1 if completed else result["start_rollout_id"])
        == result.get("num_rollout", config.miles.get("num_rollout"))
    )
)
```

四个条件的语义：① driver 没有报告完成清单（视为完成，兼容旧返回）；② 命名池耗尽（数据用尽即目标达成）；③ 不可恢复的时间停（终局停）；④ 完成计数 +1 达到总数。**关键变化在第④项右侧**：`result.get("num_rollout", config.miles.get("num_rollout"))`——driver 返回的、由原生运行时在数据加载后解析出的总数优先；编译配置里的 `num_rollout` 只是旧运行时的回退。epoch 预算 run 正是靠第④项右侧的新值被正确判为 complete。判定后 [workflow.py:424-425](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/workflow.py#L424-L425) 把 `complete`/`stopped` 与整个结果字典写进 `workflow.json`——而 4.1 里「已 complete 的 run 不可重启」正是消费这个状态。

**测试佐证**。[open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py:10-36](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py#L10-L36) 是这条链的验收：`num_epoch=2` 编译后 `miles["num_epoch"]==2` 且**没有** `num_rollout`；argv 含 `--num-epoch` 不含 `--num-rollout`；`compiled.core.save_final_checkpoint` 为真且无 `save_interval`；`training.num_rollouts` 与 `num_epoch` 并存、`num_epoch ∈ {0,-1,True}` 均抛 `ValueError`；`save_checkpoints=false` 时 `save_final_checkpoint` 不再默认为真。

**练习 1**：为什么 workflow 不干脆在编译时把 `num_epoch` 换算成 `num_rollout`？

**练习 2**：一个 epoch 预算 run 在最后一个 rollout 保存了最终权重。如果磁盘上这个存档损坏，resume 会发生什么？

**练习 3**：`result.get("num_rollout", config.miles.get("num_rollout"))` 为什么要保留后面的回退项？
**答案**：driver 与 workflow 可能来自不同版本的运行时（例如旧镜像里 driver 的返回字典还没有 `num_rollout` 字段）。此时回退到编译配置里的 `num_rollout`——rollout 预算 run 的值编译时已确定，行为与旧版完全一致。这是「新字段优先、旧字段兜底」的兼容式演进。

### 4.4 Supervisor 启动监管

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`cluster.py` 回答的问题是：**「一个 Beaker 副本内，如何把 Ray、judge 服务和训练 workflow 安全地拉起来，并在任何一方挂掉时让全体有序失败？」** `Supervisor` 是每个副本各一个的监管线程 + 子进程管理者，它提供四样东西：

- **启动预算（startup budget）**：rank 0 发布一个统一的 deadline，所有后续启动工作（inventory、judge、Ray、workflow）共享这一个时钟；
- **心跳**：每 2 秒写 `heartbeat-{rank}.json` 并检查对端心跳，超时即失败——这是「对端节点消失」的检测器；
- **子进程监管**：被监管子进程非零退出、judge 连续 3 次健康探针失败，都会让本副本失败；
- **失败可见化**：失败写 `failed-{rank}.json`，对端在 `check()` 里发现即跟着失败。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
run(config)                                  # 每个 Beaker 副本一个进程
  ├─ 编译 + topology.plan；校验副本数/排名与提交一致
  ├─ rendezvous.join(output.root/cluster/<attempt>, rank, count)
  │    → 每次启动进入全新 attempt 目录（旧的 attempt 留档）
  ├─ Supervisor(...)：rank0 写 startup.json（唯一 deadline）；其余副本等它出现
  ├─ 心跳线程启动；SIGTERM/SIGINT → 抛错（让清理路径执行）
  ├─ 各副本写 node-{rank}.json → 等全部到齐 → topology.assign 得到本机分工
  ├─ GPU inventory 校验（可见设备数 == 计划数）；rollout GPU 还要过 profile 硬件校验
  ├─ 按分工起 judge 服务（各占自己的 GPU），端点写盘；head 额外占 3 个 Ray 端口
  ├─ ray start --block（head 带 --head，worker 带 --address）
  └─ head：start_workflow（ray-readiness/judge-readiness 两个探针任务 + driver 子进程）
     其余：等 complete.json → 各写 done-{rank}.json → head 收到全部 done 后收尾
```

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**Supervisor 的构造与启动预算**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:80-107](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L80-L107)：rank 0 把 `deadline = now + startup_timeout` 写进 `startup.json`，其余副本轮询该文件直到出现（超时即失败）——**整个集群对「启动要多久」只有一个预算**，避免各副本各算各的。

**心跳线程**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:109-154](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L109-L154)：每 2 秒写自己的心跳、检查对端心跳与子进程、按需探针 judge 健康。`check_peer_heartbeats` 有两个值得注意的细节：共享文件系统上的瞬时缺文件不算对端死亡（保留最后一次观测值，但不延长其期限）；心跳超过 `heartbeat_timeout` 即抛错。被监管子进程退出码非零同样抛错——但仅当 `complete.json` 还不存在（训练完成后的退出不是故障）。

**judge 健康探针**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:156-184](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L156-L184)：judge 服务在真正 HTTP 200 之前只算「待就绪」并受启动 deadline 约束；进入稳态后每次探针失败计一次，**连续 3 次**失败才判死——容忍单次网络抖动。

**check / wait**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:195-227](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L195-L227)：`check()` 汇总所有失败源（自身线程异常、startup 任务退出、对端 `failed-*.json`）并转发子进程日志；`wait()` 在 deadline 内轮询谓词，每 30 秒打一条「还在等」的警告。注意 L206-209 的注释：**显式 timeout 只用于训练后的完成等待**——训练阶段不受启动 deadline 约束（那会误杀长训练），由 Beaker 的 run timeout 与心跳兜底。

**run：从 rendezvous 到 workflow**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:270-411](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L270-L411)：

- L283-289：以 `OI_MILES_LAUNCH_ID` 为 attempt 标识 `rendezvous.join` 到全新目录；
- L301-306：等所有 `node-{rank}.json` 到齐后由 `topology.assign` 定分工（head 取 IP 最小者）；
- L307-317：本机 GPU inventory 必须与 Beaker 分配一致，rollout GPU 还要过推理 profile 的硬件校验；
- L331-349：judge 服务逐个拉起（`SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE` 被特意移除——judge 是标准 Qwen 模型而非 Olmo 扩展），端点写入 `judge-{name}.json` 并汇入注册表环境变量；
- L357-392：`ray start --block`，head 与 worker 参数不同；
- L394-405：**只有 head 调用 `start_workflow` 并写 `complete.json`**；其余副本轮询 `complete.json`，最后全体各写 `done-{rank}.json`，head 等全部 done 再停 Ray——保证没有副本在 head 收尾时还在用 Ray。

**start_workflow：准备与就绪解耦**。[open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py:414-427](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L414-L427)：head 用 `start_task` 拉起两个**有限期**探针子进程（`--probe` 查 Ray 布局、`--probe-judges` 查 judge 就绪与 canary，见 [cluster.py:430-470](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L430-L470)），同时用 `run_child` 运行 `python -m open_instruct.miles train <config>`——即 4.1/4.2 的 workflow+driver。driver 在 `judge_readiness_wait` 阶段（[driver.py:188-189](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L188-L189)）等这些探针放行，期间可以并行做模型/数据准备。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 startup deadline 由 rank 0 统一发布，而不是各副本各自计算？
**答案**：各副本启动时刻略有先后，若各自算 deadline，先启动的先到期，会出现「A 认为 B 超时而 B 认为自己还有时间」的分歧。统一预算（[cluster.py:84-93](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L84-L93)）让所有副本对「启动窗口何时关闭」有一致视图。

**练习 2**：`start_task` 与 `start(..., monitor=True)` 有什么区别？为什么 ray-readiness 用前者、driver 用后者（`run_child`）？
**答案**：`monitor=True` 的子进程一旦非零退出就被视为崩溃（[cluster.py:238-240](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L238-L240)）；`start_task` 专门承载「有限期的启动子进程」，其退出码由 `check()` 单独汇报（[cluster.py:199-201](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L199-L201)）。driver 走 `run_child`（不进 children 列表、逐秒 `check()`）：driver 的失败要有自己的清理与失败记录路径，而不是被当作「被监管子进程崩溃」一刀切。

**练习 3**：driver 为什么要专门 `await startup.wait_ready("judges")`，而不是在起 judge 的地方同步等待？
**答案**：准备模型/数据是 CPU+IO 工作，与 judge 加载（占自己的 GPU）互不依赖。cluster 侧用探针子进程并行检测就绪（[cluster.py:422-425](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/cluster.py#L422-L425)），driver 侧在首次发布后才等 judge（[driver.py:186-189](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/execution/driver.py#L186-L189)，注释："GPU initialization and initial publication can finish while qualification runs"），把串行等待压缩成并行流水。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `workflow.execute` 把一次 run 分成准备/训练/收尾三阶段；run 身份 = 规格字典排序 JSON 的 SHA-256，resume 时只有运维字段（重试、缓存、存档/评估节奏）允许变动，模型/数据/训练视野必须严格一致。
- `driver.train` 是单次尝试的协调循环：取 batch → 优化器更新 → 存档边界 → 权重发布 → 评估分发；池耗尽、不可恢复的时间停、跑满预算三种情况算完成，debug 退出与可恢复时间停只算 stopped。
- **本轮更新**：完成判定的右侧从 `config.miles["num_rollout"]` 改为 `result.get("num_rollout", ...)`——epoch 预算的 rollout 总数由原生运行时在数据加载后解析，driver 把它带回；`training.num_epoch` 与 `num_rollouts` 互斥，编译期不再补默认 100。
- **本轮更新**：`core.save_final_checkpoint`（新 CoreConfig 字段）在 epoch 预算 + `save_checkpoints=true` 时默认置真，driver 在最后一个 rollout 落盘最终存档，替代缺失的周期 `save_interval`。
- `cluster.Supervisor` 用统一启动预算、双贴心跳（写自己 + 查对端）、judge 三连失败判死和失败文件传播，把「多副本任何一个失联」变成全体有序失败，再交给 Beaker 重试与指纹恢复闭环。

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
